title: Crusher Feed Procedure
body: The ROM pad is where mining meets processing, and it's the one spot where light vehicles, haul trucks, pedestrians, and a working loader all share the same ground. Get the approach discipline or the blend wrong and you either put someone in the line of fire or you send the wrong grade to the plant — both cost you the shift.
keyPoints: Radio first, every time. Any vehicle entering the ROM pad calls the loader operator on Channel 1 before crossing the entrance, and no radio means no entry — full stop.

The 50:30:10 GET rule is the backbone: call by radio at 50 m, inform and continue under protocol at 30 m, and never break the 10 m radius until the operator is out of the cab, visible, with the bucket grounded and radio confirmation given.

Blend is set by the foreman off the geologist's instruction, not by the operator. Current standing blend evolved to 1 SSHG + 3 MG1 (Jun 24), then 1 super + 1 SSHG + 3 MG1 (Jun 25) — but five machines was flagged as too many for the feed volume, so watch machine count against actual feed.
Hard visibility floor of 200 m. Below that, trucks return to the go-line, all ROM pad activity stops, the entrance is barricaded, and only the shift boss can give the all-clear.

Loader operator basics: enter the pile straight, bucket parallel to the floor, first gear full throttle, floor kept clean and level, and never feed with blunt GET or a bare bucket edge — that's how teeth end up in the crusher.
apply: If more than three or four machines are feeding the crusher, check whether the feed volume actually justifies it — the Jun 25 review already flagged five as overcrowding the pad, and extra machines there just multiply the interaction risk without adding throughput.
